parsed.explanation: Societal risk is moderate to elevated. Evidence shows visibly trans people in provincial cities face discrimination in public spaces and frequent physical and sexual harassment (Nov 2024). Deeply rooted stigma is documented, along with conversion practices and family exorcism, and bullying that drives people out of school. Anti-LGBTQ sentiment is described as growing, and in April 2026 supporters of the head of government sent death threats. Mitigating factors are a legal third-gender tradition, active pride events, community organisations, a capital-city support infrastructure, and school curriculum content. No violence rates are available, so the magnitude is uncertain. Visitors are less exposed to family and community pressure than residents, but harassment in public and in government settings remains a real risk, especially outside the capital.
